articles.title: PGA Tour Commissioner Currently Has No Plans to Offer LIV Golfers 'Returning Member Program'
articles.summary: Despite the uncertainty about LIV Golf's future, the PGA Tour is not planning to offer players who left to join the upstart circuit a path back.
articles.body:
Despite the uncertainty about LIV Golf's future, the PGA Tour is not planning to offer players who left to join the upstart circuit a path back.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, PGA Tour commissioner Brian Rolapp explained the Returning Member Program isn't being considered at this point that would allow LIV golfers an opportunity to back on the Tour.

"No, currently there's no current plans for [the] Returning Member Program like you saw earlier this year," Rolapp said.

Bryson's lates post raises more LIV questions

The PGA Tour adopted the Returning Member Program in January, citing fan research that showed a "clear desire" to see the best players competing more often and "timely inquiries" from non-PGA Tour players who had an interest in returning.

Under the rules of the program, players were eligible who participated in "unauthorized tournaments", have not been part on the PGA Tour for a minimum of two years and won at least one of THE PLAYERS, Masters, U.S. Open, PGA Championship and/or The Open Championship anytime between 2022 to '25.

Players had to apply for the program between Jan. 12-Feb. 2 and it only applied for the 2026 season, meaning they could not indicate now in order to return to the Tour in 2027.

The program requires participants to appear in at least 15 cosponsored and approved tournaments during the 2026 PGA Tour season. There were also financial penalties attached, including a $5 million donation to charity.

Brooks Koepka, Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith were four players who left to join LIV Golf and were offered the chance to participate. Koepka was the only one who accepted the offer.

Per The Athletic's Gabby Herzig , Koepka's estimated financial penalties could end up between $51-85 million because he won't qualify for the player equity program until 2031 and doesn't receive any share of FedEx Cup bonus money this year in addition to the charitable donation.

LIV Golf's future has been unclear in the wake of the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund announcing it was pulling its funding. LIV CEO Scott O'Neil said in a statement released on Aug. 5 that the league has an "agreement in place" with a lead investor and they "anticipate finalizing terms in the coming weeks, with the goal of entering a transaction in September" to keep it going at least through 2027.

The 2026 LIV Golf season ended one week early with an event in Indianapolis over the weekend because the planned team championship event in Michigan that would have been played from Aug. 27-30 was canceled.

It marked the second canceled event on the schedule for LIV this year. New Orleans was set to host a tournament from June 25-28 that got was officially postponed due to what it said was an attempt to "avoid the peak summer heat" in the area.

LIV Golf was founded in 2021 and played its first season the following year. The league attempted to become an alternative to the PGA Tour and signed several top stars away with incredibly lucrative contracts.

Rahm was believed to be the highest-paid player on the circuit with a deal worth $300 million, followed by Phil Mickelson at $200 million and Koepka at $130 million. DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson both received $125 million.

articles.title: Tiger Woods’ Possible Return to Golf Takes Unexpected Turn
articles.summary: Tiger Woods discussed a possible Champions Tour return with Ernie Els as his next potential golf appearance at the Nexus Cup nears. The post Tiger Woods’ Pos...
articles.body:
Tiger Woods has largely stayed away from competitive golf, but the 15-time major champion has discussed a potential return to the course.

Woods, who turned 50 in December, is now eligible for the PGA Tour Champions. While Woods has previously focused on competing against the best players on the PGA Tour, Ernie Els said in July that the two have discussed the possibility of Woods playing on the senior circuit.

According to Els, Woods wasn't simply listening to the idea. He started asking questions about it.

The update comes as Woods prepares for a potentially busy stretch in September. He is scheduled to appear in court on September 8 and could make another public appearance six days later at the Nexus Cup in New York.

Tiger Woods 'Started Warming' to PGA Tour Champions Possibility

Woods' 50th birthday opened another option for his eventual return to competitive golf.

Els, a four-time major champion who competes on the PGA Tour Champions, said he has personally discussed the possibility with Woods.

"He's always welcome; he knows that," Els said. "We had the discussion about the Champions Tour, and he asked me about it, and he started warming to it."

Woods has dealt with injuries throughout the later stages of his career, but he has continued to target the biggest events when healthy enough to compete.

The PGA Tour Champions would offer a different option now that he meets the age requirement.

"He's a busy guy; he's got a lot of responsibility," Els continued. "He's always been very busy, shifting around the last four or five years, a lot of stuff behind the scenes. I'll keep knocking on his door. I think this is the type of golf course that would really suit him."

Woods has not announced plans to join the PGA Tour Champions or set a date for a competitive return.

Woods Could Return to Golf Spotlight at September 14 Event

Before any potential competitive comeback, Woods could make a public appearance at the Nexus Cup in New York on September 14.

According to TWLegion , the charity event is connected to Woods' foundation, and he has traditionally hit golf balls for guests during the event.

Woods has made few public appearances this summer. He spent around two months at a rehabilitation facility in Switzerland before returning to the United States in June.

One of his appearances since returning came alongside PGA Tour CEO Brian Roller as the two introduced a new tour policy. Woods also attended Kai Trump's graduation celebration.

Woods has otherwise maintained a low profile while his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, undergoes treatment for breast cancer.

Tiger Woods Has September 8 Court Appearance Before Potential Golf Event

Before the Nexus Cup, Woods is scheduled to appear in court on September 8, according to TWLegion.

The appearance is connected to charges stemming from his rollover crash and DUI in late March. Woods previously waived his arraignment and requested a jury trial. His attorney, Douglas Duncan, has represented him at previous hearings.

"Tiger Woods is scheduled to appear in court for the first time on September 8th," TWLegion reported. "It has been pushed many times due to ongoing discovery in South Florida."

The latest hearing took place August 4. A July ruling allowed prosecutors to obtain hospital records connected to the crash, while the discovery process has included requests for Woods' prescription and medical records.

articles.title: PGA Tour: Changes to play-off structure for 2028 a 'big swing' says Rory McIlroy
articles.summary: Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by changing their end-of-season play-offs to matchplay.
articles.body:
Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by introducing matchplay to their end-of-season play-offs.

PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp confirmed on Thursday that from 2028 the Tour Championship will be played across two weeks, at two different courses, and adopt a head-to-head format.

World number two McIlroy, who is a three-time winner of the FedEx Cup, feels the return of matchplay to the PGA Tour for the first time since 2023 shows fans have been listened to by the decision-makers.

"I think the PGA Tour and the Future Competition Committee and Brian and everyone involved have really taken on board what the fans have been calling for and have wanted, which is matchplay," said the Northern Irishman, 37.

"Brian took me through the plan last week for the first time. I didn't really know anything about it. It's certainly different.

"Two weeks, two different venues, but it's cool. I think they've taken a big swing, and conceptually, I think I really like it."

The FedEx Cup play-offs have have gone through numerous iterations across their two decades, presently consisting of a three-event strokeplay series which begins with the top 70 players from the season-long points list.

This week's concluding Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta will have a $40m (£29.3m) purse, and while the events have undoubtedly been lucrative for players, there have been consistent questions regarding fan engagement.

McIlroy added: "I think they've been great for players. Obviously we play for a ton of money, and it's sort of like the culmination of the entire season.

"The players have been rewarded. I think what the Tour are really trying to do is listen to the fans and what they want, and I think this idea of matchplay over two weeks is something that came mostly from what the people that watch golf wanted, so I think that's a really good thing."

LIV returnees should 'eat humble pie' - Faldo Published 11 hours ago

LIV returnees should 'eat humble pie' - Faldo

'Tough road back' to PGA Tour from LIV - McIlroy Published 6 days ago

'Tough road back' to PGA Tour from LIV - McIlroy

The revised play-offs are only part of the changes coming to the PGA Tour in 2028 with a Championship and Challenger series to be established with promotion and relegation between the two.

With a regular season consisting of 15 events and a schedule which will run from February to August, McIlroy hoped more star players primarily based on the PGA Tour will follow his lead and play an increasing number of events on the DP World Tour.

The six-time major winner said: "I think if the PGA Tour are going to play from February through to August, DP World Tour have five months where, with the help of the PGA Tour and maybe some others, [it] can really shine a spotlight on international golf and put on some of the biggest international events in golf.

"I think with what the PGA Tour has been through with changing its competitive model and its structure, I think if the DP World Tour could do something similar, where you host all of your best events in that five-month time frame, it would allow guys to take up membership, to then have something to play for at the end of the DP World Tour season - if they choose to do that."

articles.title: Illinois WR Jayshon Platt likely out for start of season
articles.summary: The receiving room is getting thin.
articles.body:
As the Illini look to open the season, the team now faces some early challenges regarding injuries.

Highly touted FAU transfer Jayshon Platt will now likely miss the season opener against UAB, and potentially more.

Head coach Bret Bielema weighed in on Tuesday: "When the injury happened, we didn't know the exact timeline on it… Whether he's back week 1, week 3, or week 4, I don't really know at this point."

Platt, who came off a season where he captured 720 yards and 5 touchdowns, is viewed as one of the focal points of the Illini's offense going into this season. His talent is backed up with a recent nomination to the preseason Biletnikoff Award Watch List, which is given to the best receiver in the country.

The receiver room, under Justin Stepp, was already thinner than expected. After earlier news that FIU transfer Alex Perry will be sidelined potentially the entire season, even more weight was placed onto Platt and other receivers. Now that two critical transfer additions are sidelined, Illinois will have to look elsewhere for production.

Illinois was able to retain Collin Dixon and Hudson Clement , who will now be the headliners of this offense with the absence of Platt and Perry. I would expect these two to have a much heavier workload, especially early in the season.

Some younger, more inexperienced options may get the chance to flourish as well. Central Illinois native Brayden Trimble has been talked highly of in camp, so expect him to see the field early this season.

Illinois may also rely more than desired on the run game. With an experienced backfield full of playmakers, the coaching staff can trust this group to move the chains.

Losing another receiver is not the news fans or the coaching staff wanted to hear, especially 2 weeks before kickoff. However, Bielema has proven that he can adapt to sudden changes in playstyle and roster construction. With gameday just around the corner, it's going to be interesting to see how Illinois adjusts to these major changes.

articles.summary: Filme híbrido que mistura personagens dos Looney Toones com atores reais quase não chega aos cinemas por questões econômicas do estúdio. Produção contou com a colaboração de James Gunn.
articles.body:
"Coyote Vs. Acme", produção que mistura atores reais com personagens consagrados das animações Looney Toones, como o Pernalonga e o Patolino, demorou três anos para finalmente chegar aos cinemas, nesta quinta-feira (27). Felizmente, a espera valeu muito a pena.

A comédia amalucada estrelada por um dos personagens mais conhecidos e azarados dos desenhos animados traz todos os elementos que vão deixar os fãs de qualquer idade bem satisfeitos: uma boa história, muitos elementos que mexem com a nostalgia de quem curtiu (e ainda curte) muito esse universo e um humor acelerado e surreal. Ou seja: a diversão está garantida.

A trama é centrada em Wile E. Coyote, que, em sua eterna luta para caçar o Papa-Léguas, se cansa de ter seus planos frustrados porque todos os produtos Acme que adquire falham, o que geram consequências bombásticas (e dolorosas) para ele. Determinado a obter justiça, Wile pede ajuda ao advogado Kevin Avery (Will Forte, de "Nebraska") para levar a poderosa empresa aos tribunais.

Só que Kevin terá que lidar com Buddy Crane (John Cena, de "Velozes e Furiosos 10" ), seu ex-chefe que se tornou responsável responsável pela defesa da Acme. Em meio a situações inusitadas e inesperados segredos, Wile e Kevin precisam suportar o jogo sujo da corporação para conseguir vencer o caso.

O mais curioso em relação a "Coyote Vs. Acme" é o fato de que o longa quase não chegou a estrear nos cinemas, mesmo que a produção estivesse totalmente finalizada e pronta para ser lançada em 2023.

Após as conclusões das filmagens, o CEO (diretor-executivo) da Warner Bros. Discovery, na época, David Zaslav, decidiu que o filme deveria ficar "trancado no cofre" da empresa por causa de uma estratégia de abatimento fiscal. Além de "Coyote Vs. Acme", os longas "Batgirl" e a animação "Scooby! Um Natal Mal-Assombrado" também foram "abandonados à sorte".

Wile E. Coyote tenta mais uma vez capturar o Papa-Léguas numa cena de 'Coyote Vs. Acme' — Foto: Divulgação

A decisão fez com que o diretor do filme, Dave Green (de "As Tartarugas Ninjas: Fora das Sombras") mandasse uma mensagem nas suas redes sociais lamentando a medida. O texto causou comoção entre os fãs, que iniciaram uma campanha para que "Coyote Vs. Acme" deixasse o limbo e conseguisse ser lançado.

Por causa disso e também devido à pressão da indústria cinematográfica, a Warner voltou atrás (em parte) e permitiu que outros distribuidores adquirissem os direitos da produção. Depois de algumas tentativas frustradas com algumas empresas como Netflix, Amazon, Paramount e Sony, que não fizeram ofertas que agradassem ao estúdio do Pernalonga, o acordo finalmente saiu com a independente Ketchup Entertainment em 2025. O valor oficial da aquisição não foi divulgado, mas especula-se que o gasto tenha sido entre US$ 50 milhões e US$ 75 milhões.

Assim, "Coyote Vs. Acme" conseguiu finalmente o seu lançamento mundial em 2026 e a Ketchup fez muito bem em salvar o filme. Seria uma pena se o grande público não tivesse a oportunidade de ver e curtir essa obra que certamente vai agradar ao público dos 8 aos 80 anos.

Wile E. Coyote, seu advogado Kevin Avery (Will Forte) e sua parceira Paige Avery (Lana Condor) numa cena de em 'Coyote vs Acme' — Foto: Divulgação

O bom roteiro, escrito por Samy Burch, a partir de um argumento de Jeremy Slater (de “Mortal Kombat 2”) e James Gunn (sim, ele mesmo, de “Guardiões da Galáxia” e “Superman”), além do próprio Burch, trabalha bem os elementos que geralmente aparecem em filmes de tribunal.

Assim, temos o advogado idealista disposto a lutar até o fim contra uma corporação poderosa e corrupta, a relação que vai se tornando uma verdadeira amizade entre o defensor e seu cliente, além dos golpes e armações feitos pela grande empresa para manter as coisas como estão. Tudo isso feito com muito bom humor e ironia, como nos desenhos antigos.

E, claro, o filme também aproveita a oportunidade de usar a grande quantidade de personagens clássicos das animações da Warner e os coloca em cena de uma forma bastante eficaz. Seja numa curta participação (do tipo “piscou, perdeu”) ou mesmo com bem mais tempo de cena. Claro que os mais famosos, como o Pernalonga, o Patolino e o Piu-Piu, além do Coyote e do Papa-Léguas, claro, aparecem bem mais no longa. Mas os coadjuvantes também surgem para dar o seu recado, mesmo que rapidamente, de uma forma que não soa gratuita ou desnecessária.

Wile E. Coyote, Paige (Lana Condor) e Kevin (Will Forte) numa cena de 'Coyote Vs. Acme' — Foto: Divulgação

É curioso, também, que o filme faça uma inusitada (e, por que não, merecida) homenagem ao ator Peter Lorre, que hoje é praticamente um desconhecido, mas que trabalhou em filmes importantes para o cinema, como os clássicos “M, o Vampiro de Dusseldorf” (1931), “Relíquia Macabra” (1941) e “Casablanca”(1942). Os cinéfilos certamente vão gostar dessa referência.

O diretor Dave Green também faz um trabalho exemplar tanto no humor quanto em fazer os atores “interagirem” com os personagens animados. Os bons efeitos visuais fazem com que tudo o que aparece na tela pareça natural, por mais surreal que seja. É claro, não supera o que Robert Zemeckis realizou no clássico “Uma Cilada Para Roger Rabbit” (1988), ainda o melhor filme a misturar pessoas reais com animações, mas mostra um resultado bem mais competente do que o decepcionante “Space Jam: Um Novo Legado” (2022).

O cineasta também se beneficia do bom elenco para obter o ótimo resultado que se vê em “Coyote Vs. Acme. Especialmente com Will Forte como o protagonista de bom coração. O ator consegue convencer na honestidade de seu personagem, que, mesmo morrendo de medo das consequências que pode sofrer, não desiste de lutar por sua causa, nem por seu cliente, por mais que ele seja um tanto imprevisível.

Buddy Crane (John Cena) leva uma encarada do Frangolino numa cena de 'Coyote Vs. Acme' — Foto: Divulgação

O astro John Cena parece estar se especializando em fazer brucutus com más intenções, mas com uma forte veia cômica. E, aqui, ele se sai muito bem. As cenas que faz ao lado do Frangolino (que no filme é o chefão da Acme!) são bem divertidas graças ao seu carisma. Já Lana Condor (a Jubileu de “X-Men: Apocalipse”), não tem muito o que fazer a não ser o braço direito do personagem de Forte. Não atrapalha, mas também não se destaca.

Com um desfecho um pouco previsível, mas ao mesmo tempo tocante (não se surpreenda se alguém chorar no escurinho do cinema), “Coyote Vs. Acme” justifica toda a mobilização que teve para que não ficasse perdido no limbo e jamais fosse visto pelo grande público. E mostra que os personagens clássicos dos Looney Tunes ainda têm bastante força e energia mesmo nos dias de hoje. Basta que eles sejam parte de um bom projeto que eles sempre vão arrasar e divertir. Na telinha ou na telona.

articles.title: PGA chief says 'no current plans' for LIV stars to return
articles.summary: The PGA currently has no plans to offer LIV Golf stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm a pathway back from the struggling breakaway tour, chief executive...
articles.body:
The PGA currently has no plans to offer LIV Golf stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm a pathway back from the struggling breakaway tour, chief executive officer Brian Rolapp said Tuesday.

Launched in 2022, LIV caused shockwaves in the golf world as it spent billions of dollars luring top players away from the traditional PGA, but its survival is now deeply uncetain.

Having lost their Saudi investors, LIV organizers have promised a slimmed-down "2.0" version next year with new investors, but several key players have been linked with exits.

While the PGA Tour offered a temporary path back for some LIV players -- five-time major winner Brooks Koepka in January took advantage, paying financial penalties -- no repeats are planned, said Rolapp.

"Currently there's no current plans for Returning Member Program like you saw earlier this year," he said, ahead of this week's season-ending Tour Championship in Atlanta, Georgia.

The PGA has banned LIV players from its events, insisting any player wishing to return must first entirely cut ties with LIV, and Rolapp told Tuesday's press conference that "rules matter."

"Accountability and discipline are essential to any organization, and certainly for the integrity of the TOUR and for the game," he said.

Rolapp said it was impossible to speculate on if and how other LIV players could one day return to the PGA because "I don't know the future of LIV."

"We've been consistent. Anyone who's interested in coming to the PGA TOUR needs to demonstrate that they are relieved of their contractual commitments or any tail obligations they might have in that legacy model," he said.

"Brooks certainly did that, and until then, we weren't really able to consider anything seriously. I would say the same thing here."

LIV organizers have vowed to return next year with a slimmed-down schedule, smaller prizes and new investors.

Speaking at LIV's season-ending Indianapolis event Sunday, DeChambeau said he was "proud" of what the tour has achieved, and said he had "great thoughts about what could happen next year."

But on Monday he published an enigmatic post on Instagram -- photos of several LIV victories, with the caption "It was a good run."

articles.title: Golf giant Callaway apologizes after ad sparks outcry
articles.summary: Golf equipment giant Callaway issued an apology on Tuesday for a now-cancelled advert which showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when s...
articles.body:
Golf equipment giant Callaway issued an apology on Tuesday for a now-cancelled advert which showed a male golfer shoving a female player to the ground when she reaches for his new driver.

The commercial, which was released online last week before being pulled, triggered a backlash over its depiction of violence against women, in addition to calls for a boycott of Callaway products.

Callaway golf chief executive Chip Brewer said in a statement on Tuesday that the company had launched an investigation into how the advert -- produced by golf media firm Good Good Golf -- had been approved.

"Last week Good Good Golf and Callaway posted a video to promote a co-branded driver," Brewer said in a statement.

"While the video was produced by Good Good, it was approved by Callaway prior to posting. That approval should never have happened. Mistakes were made and we are taking the matter very seriously.

"As we deal with the consequences of our mistake and complete our investigations, I want to make it clear that we sincerely apologize for the video.

"The content was inappropriate and does not reflect our values. To be clear: we are unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence or threatening behavior of any kind... I assure you we will learn from this and do better."

The online advert showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark barging Epson Tour professional player Alexis Miestowski to the ground when she attempts to reach for his driver, before warning her: "Do not touch my new driver."

Good Good Golf, which centers its business around a successful YouTube channel aimed at bringing a younger audience to the sport, had already apologized for the controversial advert.

"We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand," Good Good said in a statement.

"We have since taken that content down. And sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward."

Good Good's rise will see the company be the title sponsor for the PGA Tour's inaugural Good Good Championship in Austin, Texas in November.

PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp said on Tuesday the circuit was dismayed by the advert and Good Good's handling of the controversy.

"I think what we saw was concerning, is clearly not aligned with PGA TOUR values. We take it very seriously," Rolapp said.

"I think their initial response was disappointing. It was a bit defensive and late.

"But I think the responses are getting better. I think we've seen some things this morning, we've had some conversations with them, so we'll continue to monitor and work with them going forward. But no, we were disappointed with what we saw."

articles.title: Seve Ballesteros Mastered Speed With One Clever Putting Trick
articles.summary: Discover the specific putting adjustment Seve Ballesteros used to control green speed and cut down three-putts, according to new reporting from Golf.com.
articles.body:
Seve Ballesteros changed how the game was played on the greens. His ability to read speed was legendary, but it wasn't magic. It was a specific trick he used to dial in his distance and reduce those costly three-putts. This method allowed the Spanish legend to navigate fast surfaces with a feel that others could not match. The story of his technique has resurfaced in recent coverage, shedding light on a skill that defined his career.

According to Golf.com, Seve Ballesteros used this clever trick on the greens to dial in his speed. Melton notes that Ballesteros focused intensely on reducing three-putts through this specific adjustment. The article places the story in the "Latest In Instruction" section, indicating its value for modern players looking to improve. Melton, the associate game-improvement editor for GOLF.com, has deep roots in the sport, having worked with the Texas Golf Association and the PGA Tour before joining the team. His reporting confirms that the trick was not about power, but about a refined sense of touch and rhythm.

The technique involved a deliberate approach to the stroke that many amateurs overlook. Instead of trying to muscle the ball, Ballesteros relied on a smooth pendulum motion that felt natural. This allowed him to trust his read completely. When a player trusts their read, they stop fighting the line and start flowing with it. That is where the speed control comes from. It's a simple concept, but executing it under pressure requires years of practice. Ballesteros spent those years perfecting the art of the lag putt. He understood that getting close was more important than making the hole every time. This mindset shifted the entire game for him.

The relevance of Ballesteros' method remains strong in the modern game. Even with advanced technology and laser readings, the human element on the greens cannot be replaced. Players today still struggle with speed control, often leaving putts short or long. The core issue is usually a lack of feel, which is exactly what Ballesteros cultivated. His trick forced him to slow down and focus on the quality of the stroke rather than the result. This is a lesson that applies to any golfer, from the weekend hacker to the Tour professional. By adopting a similar mindset, players can lower their scores without changing their equipment. The mental shift is often the biggest hurdle.

Experts agree that feel is the hardest skill to teach. You can't measure it with a launch monitor. It comes from repetition and confidence. Ballesteros built that confidence through his unique routine. He treated every putt as a test of his own patience and rhythm. This approach allowed him to handle the most stressful situations on the biggest stages. The trick wasn't a secret device or a strange grip change. It was a mental discipline that translated into physical execution. That's why it still resonates with golfers decades after his passing. The fundamentals of speed control haven't changed, even if the courses have.

The next step for golfers interested in this style is to practice the feel, not just the mechanics. Zephyr Melton's reporting on Golf.com serves as a reminder that the greatest players often had the simplest solutions.

articles.title: Joining the Miami Heat is a 'match made in heaven' for Klay Thompson
articles.summary: Klay Thompson seems to have found the perfect fit for him in Miami.
articles.body:
Joining the Miami Heat is a 'match made in heaven' for Klay Thompson originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

After years of struggles, the Miami Heat have finally gotten serious with their roster construction. They sent the Milwaukee Bucks a significant trade package to acquire superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo . Since the trade involved a lot of players going away, they need more reinforcements.

One of those reinforcements has finally arrived in the form of four-time champion Klay Thompson . He was a star player on the dominant Golden State Warriors alongside Stephen Curry and Draymond Green , who won four titles together.

Klay Thompson believes he found the perfect match with the Miami Heat

The 2026-27 NBA season is set for a blockbuster campaign for a lot of teams, especially in the Eastern Conference. Miami is just one of the teams that have improved their roster, as this also includes the superteam the Philadelphia 76ers are rolling out with the addition of Jaylen Brown and LeBron James .

The Heat have received considerable attention, but it is not on the same level as the 76ers . It can work in the Heat's favor because they can surprise a lot of people, especially with how people spoke about their lack of perimeter shooting. Now, they have one of the greatest shooters of all time in Thompson.

MORE: The reason why Klay Thompson chose to sign with the Heat amid all the offers

As a four-time champion, Thompson knows how to win. Now that he is on the Heat, it seems this is the perfect fit for him. He was unhappy with his chances of winning with the Dallas Mavericks , especially since he thought Luka Doncic would be there for the long term. Now, he is on the Heat looking to win another one.

"I just missed out on the postseason. I hate watching from home. You get FOMO watching all your coworkers just getting to chase their dreams, and it's not fun not making the playoffs. That's all I want to do these next couple years. Have a chance to make a deep postseason run," Thompson said about the Heat being the perfect match in his interview with Brendan Tobin .

"So excited to be in Miami. They're a very demanding organization, but I love being in that ultra-competitive atmosphere, and this was a match made in heaven."

Playing for the Heat comes with extra pressure for most players. However, that is not the case for Thompson because he is quite familiar with the responsibilities he has in Miami. He managed to win four titles in the past, this time, he wants to contribute to win his fifth and help the Heat succeed again.

articles.title: Buen invento mal parido
articles.standfirst: El LIV Golf 1.0 echó el cierre. Seguramente habrá una nueva versión, pero ya no será la misma. En el Excel fue más de lo que realmente ha sido
articles.summary: El LIV Golf 1.0 echó el cierre. Seguramente habrá una nueva versión, pero ya no será la misma. En el Excel fue más de lo que realmente ha sido
articles.body: Se nota un aire casi de victoria entre los detractores del LIV Golf por la manera en la que ha acabado el circuito en su primera era, seguramente la que más titulares arranque en su historia. Durante cinco temporadas, desde junio de 2022, la alternativa impulsada desde el Fondo Público de Arabia Saudí (PIF) fue un sueño y una pesadilla a la vez, para terminar como los amores de verano, siendo un recuerdo interrumpido una noche de agosto. El LIV quiso ser vendido como un avance hacia la modernidad del golf, un deporte poco acostumbrado al cambio. Un circuito mundial de verdad a 54 hoyos, resuelta la jornada en menos de cinco horas, jugado en bermudas y con música y con el aliciente de unos premios que han roto el mercado. El legado que ha dejado es más profundo que los interesados análisis que se hacen. El LIV no ha salido derrotado. Arabia, simplemente, ha perdido el interés en el golf porque les ha salido por un ojo: 5.600 millones de dólares. Hay cuestiones que respaldan la aventura, dirán los defensores. El golf ha confirmado mercados apasionantes como Australia y Sudáfrica, cuyos grandes eventos no seducían ya a las estrellas y que han vuelto a primera línea. La música y el hoyo desparrame —que ya exístía en Phoenix, sí— son otros alicientes para atraer a otro público menos tradicional. Futbolizarlo. Que podrá sonar a crítica, pero es que el fútbol es el deporte más popular del mundo. Y lo de la salida a tiro, es una manera más justa de resolver torneos, no tan pendientes de los partes meteorológicos. Las cosas que se han hecho mal, dirán sus opositores, provocarán heridas en el golf. Seguramente. Rahm, que fue el campeón las tres temporadas, ha ganado más de 90 millones en premios en este ciclo. Y ha jugado 40 torneos. Es un botín desorbitado que ha tenido un efecto contagio —defensivo— en el PGATour. Las ganancias de los golfistas están por encima de lo que genera la industria. Se quiso dar mucho valor a los equipos, pero se alumbró mal desde el momento en el que el ganador individual ganaba más que por escuadras. Tampoco se premió la meritocracia de una manera clara. No se sabe cómo será el 2.0, pero a priori da la sensación de que será un sucedáneo. Y si es sin Rahm y sin DeChambeau, algo demasiado menor.

articles.title: Green light as Liverpool close in on record forward deal
articles.summary: Liverpool are expected to be busy in the final stages of this summer’s transfer window. Despite a poor midfield showing against Newcastle in Andoni Iraola’s...
articles.body:
Liverpool are expected to be busy in the final stages of this summer's transfer window.

Despite a poor midfield showing against Newcastle in Andoni Iraola 's Premier League opener on Sunday the Reds are unlikely to go into the market for a specialist No6.

Instead the focus will be on improving the frontline further. Liverpool used Rio Ngumoha and Cody Gakpo as their wide forward starting options against the Toon at St. James' Park.

It's simply not enough for Iraola and sporting director Richard Hughes however - who are still reeling from the loss of Mohamed Salah on a free transfer to Trabzonspor.

Deals are live for several forward - per reports - with Yankuba Minteh and Ibrahim Mbaye said to be under consideration.

The 2024/25 Premier League champions have spent all summer however pursuing a deal for Bradley Barcola .

The France international, 23, is not currently among Paris Saint-Germain's options as his future is sorted out. The two-time European champion remains under contract at Parc des Princes until 2028.

With no new deal on the horizon it looks as though Luis Enrique's side will have to cash in .

L'Equipe is now reporting that Barcola's entourage are confident of securing the move they want this summer which is a transfer to Liverpool. There are also signs of movement on PSG's valuation of their versatile winger.

Originally the French aristocrats were seeking a deal worth £145m for Barcola but it looks as though that price will come down dramatically as a deal is sought in the closing stages of the transfer window.

Barcola to Liverpool will be a PSG club-record deal

The Parisians are expected to bank a club-record fee for Barcola - surpassing the €90m paid for Neymar by Al-Hilal back in 2023.

It will still be a reasonable deal from a Liverpool perspective for their No1 target - albeit the most expensive outbound deal in French Ligue 1 history.

That record currently stands at the €100m Manchester City paid to Lille for Ayyoub Bouaddi - with PSG already turning down bids worth €115m by the Merseysiders.

However the pressure on PSG will grow as a resolution on Barcola's future is sought.

Barcola wants Liverpool, Liverpool want Barcola and PSG might have to accept slightly less than they were originally asking for. It looks as though Liverpool will get the green light soon.

articles.title: ‘What About [Jalen] Hurts?’ — Packers Star Micah Parsons’ Brother Ridicules Eagles QB’s Ugly INT in Practice
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts has plenty to prove as the Philadelphia Eagles prepare for another season with the privileged burden of expectations firmly on the Super Bowl LIX...
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts has plenty to prove as the Philadelphia Eagles prepare for another season with the privileged burden of expectations firmly on the Super Bowl LIX champions.

A new offensive coordinator has brought changes, but Hurts has endured a difficult stretch during training camp. Now, a mistake in practice has given Micah Parsons ' brother a chance to join the conversation around Philadelphia's quarterback.

Micah Parsons' Brother Takes Aim at Jalen Hurts' Pick-Six

Hurts' latest turnover came during a practice session at Lincoln Financial Field, where cornerback Riq Woolen intercepted him twice. The second pick became a touchdown, and the play made its way onto social media after Philly sports personality Victor Williams posted a video of it on X.

Terrence Parsons Jr., the brother of Green Bay Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons, reshared the clip with a short message aimed directly at Hurts.

"What about Hurts lmfaoooo," Terrence wrote.

The post arrived during a difficult stretch for Hurts, who has struggled with turnovers while Philadelphia installs a revamped offense under coordinator Sean Mannion. His recent practices have included several interceptions, giving opponents and fans plenty to discuss before the regular season begins.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Hurts also had a rough two-day stretch against the New England Patriots, throwing five interceptions across joint practices. He had three interceptions in one session while finishing 19-of-27 without a touchdown during Aug. 19's practice.

Through 16 practices this summer, Hurts has thrown 13 interceptions. The figure stands out because he threw just 15 across his previous four training camps combined.

Still, Hurts' regular-season track record provides important context. In 2025, he completed 64.8% of his passes for 3,224 yards, 25 touchdowns, and six interceptions. He also ran for 421 yards and eight touchdowns, making his dual-threat ability a key part of Philadelphia's offense.

The Eagles will begin their regular season Sept. 13 against the Washington Commanders , giving Hurts a short window to turn the narrative around.

The social media criticism certainly paints a bad picture for Hurts, and his response should come once Philadelphia opens its season. His interceptions from practice won't count then, but he will have to improve in the games that matter to climb up from last season's 16th position in PFN's NFL QB Impact ranking.

articles.title: 'If my mind is free, half the game is won': Mohammad Azhar finds his breakthrough at Kolar Open
articles.summary: Golf News: NEW DELHI: For six years, Mohammad Azhar has quietly chased improvement rather than applause. The Kolar Open champion may have finally lifted one of t.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For six years, Mohammad Azhar has quietly chased improvement rather than applause. The Kolar Open champion may have finally lifted one of the biggest titles of his professional career, but ask him what changed since turning pro in 2020 and his answer isnât about trophies, rankings or prize money.âThe biggest improvement in my game has been my driver,â Azhar said. âEarlier, I used to hit a lot of duck hooks. Now Iâm able to hit controlled shots, and that gave me confidence.âThat confidence became the foundation of his triumph at the Kolar Open, where the Hyderabad-based golfer produced four remarkably composed rounds without ever allowing the occasion to dictate his game. Ironically, winning was never part of the plan.âI never thought about winning. My only focus was to keep following my process every day.âItâs an approach that sounds simple but reflects one of golfâs hardest lessons, resisting the temptation to think about the leaderboard.Born in Mathura and settled in Hyderabad for nearly a decade, Azharâs journey into golf began with family. His elder brother, Mohammad Arek, introduced him to the sport while coaching at the Army Golf Course in Mathura. That relationship shaped not only his swing but also his life.âMy brother taught me golf. Heâs no longer with us,â Azhar says softly, recalling the accident that claimed his brotherâs life. âAfter he passed away, I left Mathura and moved to Hyderabad. It was his dream.âToday, Azhar competes without a personal coach, relying instead on experience, self-belief and the support of people who believed in him during difficult years.âSo many people including Hyderabad golf association all members and Rupinder Singh Gill helped meâ he says. âSomeone gifted me irons, someone gave me a driver, others helped with tournament expenses and sponsorships. I canât even count all the names.âAmong those closest to his journey is the Hyderabad Golf Association, which he calls his âhome turfâ and credits for providing a platform to grow.His victory at Kolar was built on precision rather than aggression. The driver, once his biggest weakness, became his greatest weapon as he repeatedly found fairways across four rounds.âI think I won with my driver,â he says. âI hardly missed the fairway.âYet the defining moment arrived in the final round, when Azhar began two shots behind the leader. Instead of chasing birdies, he slowed himself down literally.âI control my breathing. I donât walk fast, I donât become overexcited. When my breathing is under control, my mind stays cool.âThat breathing routine has become his reset button during pressure situations. He admits there were tournaments in the past where he led by two or three shots and still failed to convert because his mind drifted toward the trophy instead of the next shot.âIâve been in that situation before,â he says. âThe moment I started thinking about winning, I stopped following my process.âAt Kolar, his target was refreshingly modest: finish every round under par.âWhether it was one-under or five-under didnât matter. I just wanted to be under par every day.âThe victory also comes at a fascinating time for Indian golf. The partnership between the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) and DP World has significantly raised prize purses and created new opportunities for domestic professionals.Azhar believes the impact is already visible.âThe competition has increased a lot because the prize money has gone up,â he says. âMore players are interested now, and everyone wants to compete.âBut he also points to a reality that often goes unnoticed. While international golfers arrive with multiple sponsors printed across their shirts, many Indian professionals step onto the first tee carrying financial worries alongside their golf bags.âYouâll see foreign players with three or four sponsor logos,â he says. âTheyâre free-minded and enjoy their golf. Weâre often thinking about making the cut, earning money and travelling to the next event. That pressure stays in our heads.âFor Azhar, greater sponsorship isnât merely about comfort itâs about unlocking performance.âIf my mind is free, half the game is already won,â he says.As he prepares for the next stretch of the PGTI season, that philosophy remains unchanged. Rankings, titles and qualification dreams for bigger tours are important, but they remain secondary to the daily discipline that carried him to Kolar.Indian golf is steadily expanding its global footprint, and players like Mohammad Azhar represent its resilient middle ground, talented enough to win, grounded enough to know that success is rarely built on one spectacular shot. Sometimes, it begins with something as quiet as a controlled breath, a fairway found, and the patience to trust the process.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Indiaâs Golf season gets new look as PGTI unveils race to championship
articles.summary: Golf News: NEW DELHI: Indian professional golf is set for a major shake-up with the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) unveiling the Race to India Championsh.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian professional golf is set for a major shake-up with the Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI) unveiling the Race to India Championship, a season-long competition that will decide the 2026 Order of Merit champion while adding greater significance to the country's richest golf tournament.The new format aligns the domestic tour more closely with the international calendar and creates a clearer pathway for India's leading golfers to graduate onto the global circuit.Unlike previous seasons, the PGTI Order of Merit title will now be decided only after the India Championship, scheduled at Delhi Golf Club from October 15 to 18. The US$4 million event will serve as the decisive season finale rather than a standalone marquee tournament.The Race will comprise nine tournaments offering a combined prize purse of Rs 10 crore, taking the total prize money across the 2026 PGTI season to Rs 41 crore. The first three events - the J&K Open, Coal India Open and Kolar Open, have already been completed, with the Telangana Open beginning the next phase of the Race this week.The season-long contest will culminate with the inaugural Kapil Dev Invitational Tour Championship at Jaypee Greens, Greater Noida, from September 30 to October 3.At the conclusion of that event, two key milestones will be confirmed: the top 24 players on the Race standings will qualify for the India Championship, while the top 60 on the PGTI Order of Merit will secure full playing rights for the 2027 season.PGTI President Kapil Dev believes the revamped structure will reward consistency throughout the season instead of placing emphasis on isolated performances.âThis introduces a fascinating season-long contest that raises the competitive standard and further enhances the significance of the India Championship. Aligning our calendar with the international tour also gives our leading players a better opportunity to make an immediate impact internationally,â Kapil Dev said.Another significant change is the tour calendar itself. From 2026 onwards, the PGTI season will conclude in October instead of stretching into December, bringing it in sync with the international schedule. The synchronisation means the Indian Order of Merit champion can transition directly onto the international circuit after earning exempt status, maximising playing opportunities without a lengthy off-season.The nine tournaments in the inaugural Race include stops in Srinagar, Kolkata, Kolar, Vikarabad, Hyderabad, Chennai, Nava Raipur, Bengaluru and Greater Noida. While the Golconda Masters returns for its 12th edition, the Chennai Open and Bengaluru Open continue their revival, and both the Nava Raipur Open and Kapil Dev Invitational Tour Championship make their debut on the professional circuit.The Race also adds fresh intrigue to the closing stretch of the domestic season, with every event carrying implications for qualification as well as the Order of Merit standings. Players will battle not only for tournament titles but also for coveted places in the elite 24-player field at the India Championship.Following the conclusion of the Delhi showpiece, the 2027 PGTI season will begin immediately, marking the start of the next Race and establishing October as the new turning point in Indian professional golf.As part of the season-ending celebrations, Delhi Golf Club will also host a Pro-Am a day after the championship, followed by the annual awards ceremony where the PGTI Order of Merit Champion and the Emerging Player of the Year will be honoured, bringing the curtain down on a season designed to redefine the road to golfing glory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Houston Rockets' Shrewd Negotiating Could Extend Their Title Window
articles.summary: The more that the Rockets get their core players signed to team-friendly contracts, the better chance they'll have of remaining in the NBA's championship pic...
articles.body:
While other teams around the NBA were busy making blockbuster moves this offseason, the Houston Rockets only made a pair of minor additions. They signed veteran guard Marcus Smart to a two-year, $12.4 million contract using the taxpayer mid-level exception (which hard-capped them at the second apron) and added veteran wing Bogdan Bogdanović on a one-year, veteran-minimum contract.

The Rockets' most notable move was signing restricted free agent Tari Eason to a five-year, $81.5 million contract. That was a continuation of a trend that might help extend the Rockets' championship window.

Since the NBA's latest collective bargaining agreement went into effect in 2023, the Rockets have arguably been the league's most shrewd team in contract negotiations. As other teams start to face financial reckonings in fear of the punitive second apron , the Rockets have locked up most of their core on team-friendly contracts.

If they're able to continue that trend moving forward, it could give them a clear advantage over their Western Conference counterparts who've been handing out max contracts without thinking twice.

The Rockets put the league on notice when they agreed to extensions with 2021 No. 2 overall pick Jalen Green and No. 16 overall pick Alperen Şengün ahead of the rookie-scale extension deadline in October 2024.

Şengün was coming off a season in which he averaged a career-high 21.1 points, 9.3 rebounds and 5.0 assists. Under the NBA's previous CBA, he likely would have been a no-brainer max-contract player. Instead, he wound up settling for nearly $40 million less than what he could have received from the Rockets as a free agent.

Meanwhile, Green agreed to a three-year, $105.3 million extension with a third-year player option. ESPN's Shams Charania noted he was the first player "ever to successfully negotiate a 2-plus-1 rookie extension on a nine-figure deal" and that the player option gave Green "the ability to increase his earning potential down the road." However, Green was the only top-four pick from the 2021 draft not to get a full five-year max deal even though he averaged nearly 20 points per game across his first three seasons.

Why did the Rockets play hardball with both Şengün and Green when other teams were handing out massive contracts to 2021 first-round picks that offseason? They might have been concerned about Green's dismal efficiency—he shot only 42.1% across his first three seasons—and Şengün's defensive ability and lack of three-point shooting. By giving them below-max deals, they hedged their bets on both players.

The following offseason, the Rockets included Green in their trade package for 15-time All-Star and two-time NBA champion Kevin Durant . Had the Rockets signed Green to a max extension, it's unclear whether the Phoenix Suns would have been as amenable to taking him as part of the return for Durant.

Not even Durant was spared from the Rockets' negotiating prowess, though. Upon his arrival in Houston, he was eligible to sign a two-year extension worth roughly $120 million . Instead, the Rockets locked him up on a two-year, $90 million deal that's worth less than 27% of the salary cap each season.

One week after the Rockets agreed to trade for Durant, they came to terms with 2022 No. 3 overall pick Jabari Smith Jr. on a five-year, $122 million contract. It begins at $23.6 million this coming season, drops to $21.75 million next year—we'll circle back to that shortly—before going back up by $1.9 million in each of the final three seasons. Smith is never projected to earn more than 15% of the salary cap in any year of his deal.

Eason's contract is even more of a steal. It ascends by roughly $1.1 million every season and is never projected to be worth even 10% of the salary cap . His starting salary ($14.05 million) is roughly $1 million less than the non-taxpayer mid-level exception ($15.044 million) this year.

According to ESPN's Brian Windhorst , the Rockets offered Eason a five-year deal worth more than $100 million ahead of the rookie-scale extension deadline last fall, although Windhorst clarified that he didn't know "how much of it would have been guaranteed." ESPN's Tim MacMahon later revealed that the Rockets' offer contained only $65 million of guaranteed money, so Eason secured more guaranteed money with his new contract, even if the overall value is lower.

That shrewd negotiating has the Rockets in a healthy place financially moving forward. In 2027-28, Şengün, Smith and Eason are set to earn only $74.2 million combined, while Durant has a $46.1 million player option. They have an additional $19.2 million tied up in Steven Adams and Clint Capela , while Reed Sheppard will be earning $14.0 million in the final year of his rookie-scale deal.

The Rockets aren't out of the woods yet, though. In fact, their toughest negotiations may still lie ahead.

While the Rockets already signed Eason to an extension, he wasn't their only first-round pick in 2023. They spent the No. 4 overall pick on Amen Thompson, who has quickly developed into a cornerstone in Houston.

This past season, Thompson set new career highs in points (18.3), assists (5.3), steals (1.5) and minutes (37.4) per game. He also averaged 7.8 rebounds, which was third on the team behind only Şengün and Adams. After earning a first-team All-Defense nod and finishing fifth in the Defensive Player of the Year race in 2024-25, Thompson was eighth in DPOY voting last season.

The only problem is that he's a dismal three-point shooter. Through the first three years of his career, he's gone 58-of-265 (21.9%) from deep. Until he becomes more of a threat from three-point range, opponents will sag off him and dare him to beat them from distance, especially in the playoffs.

Şengün's lack of three-point shooting only compounds that issue for the Rockets. Having two non-shooters in the starting five might be Houston's Achilles' heel unless Şengün and/or Thompson drastically improve their efficiency from deep.

That could complicate Thompson's ongoing extension talks, too. The Rockets have until Oct. 19 to sign him to a rookie-scale extension. If Thompson doesn't agree to one by then, he'll become a restricted free agent in 2027.

In mid-May, Varun Shankar of the Houston Chronicle warned that the Rockets were unlikely to give Thompson a max extension.

"Such a contract would pay him a quarter of the salary cap over the next few seasons, but the impressive guard/forward still faces enough questions about his shot and eventual offensive profile," Shankar wrote. "That, combined with the Rockets' precedent of getting relatively team-friendly extensions (see Şengün, Alperen, above) should keep him in the ballpark of 20-23% of the salary cap."

The Rockets could always decide to table extension talks and let Thompson become a restricted free agent, although they'd run the risk of another team offering him a full max contract next offseason. Waiting would allow them to see what happens with VanVleet , who's set to become an unrestricted free agent, and Durant, who could join VanVleet in unrestricted free agency by declining his $46.1 million player option.

Long-term, the Rockets also need to be budgeting for Sheppard, who becomes extension-eligible next offseason. Internally, they believe Sheppard "has the potential to develop into an all-time great, such as former Phoenix Suns point guard Steve Nash , if given enough time and the right conditions," according to MacMahon and ESPN's Ramona Shelburne .

Juggling all of these financial considerations helps explain why the Rockets weren't more aggressive this offseason as Giannis Antetokounmpo , Jaylen Brown , Kawhi Leonard and LaMelo Ball all changed hands via trade. A "high-ranking Rockets source" told MacMahon and Shelburne that they were "hyperfocused" on their young core and didn't feel win-now pressure despite having Durant on their roster.

"Our five guys have a chance to win a lot of games together for a long time," the source added. "We don't want to make the mistake other teams have of giving up on guys too soon. We want a 10-year run."

The second-apron era is shortening title windows across the league, so a 10-year run might not be realistic for the Rockets or any other team. But the more that the Rockets get their core players signed to team-friendly, well-below-max contracts, the better chance they'll have of remaining in the championship picture.

articles.title: Patrick Cantlay disagrees with Jack Nicklaus’ opinion about the golf ball rollback
articles.summary: The ever-increasing distance in modern-day golf is threatening the future of the game. The pace of technological advancement is unsustainable.
articles.body:
The ever-increasing distance in modern-day golf is threatening the future of the game.

The pace of technological advancement is unsustainable. Historic venues such as St Andrews are constantly having to reinvent themselves to keep up with the distances players can now achieve, and that's if they haven't already been rendered obsolete in pro golf.

One way this issue is being tackled is the golf ball rollback. New rules are set to be introduced around the golf ball, which should take some distance away from the players. There has been widespread debate about how effective this new golf ball will be, but many players agree change is necessary.

Among those players is Jack Nicklaus, who has been waving the warning flag on this issue for a number of years. However, his opinion isn't shared by all. Patrick Cantlay argued at the Tour Championship that there's no need for a golf ball rollback at all.

Patrick Cantlay is not in support of the golf ball rollback

There have been a few players to declare their opposition to the golf ball rollback, and Cantlay is among them.

Speaking before the Tour Championship, he was asked about a recent meeting on the issue and explained why he's not in favour of the change.

He said, "I'm definitely encouraged. We had a good meeting. There was a PAC meeting earlier this year at Memorial, and the USGA and the R&A were there and talked with a number of players.

"I'm not in support of rolling the golf ball back. I think the game is in a really good spot. We have more rounds of golf being played each and every year in this country and more new golfers that are playing golf.

"I think the guys are hitting it farther because they're trying to hit it farther, and they're training to hit it farther. The guys are bigger and stronger.

"I don't think we need to do something massive like change the golf ball. I think that would just — I don't think the pros outweigh the cons there."

Players have said the golf ball rollback won't decrease distance enough to be worth the time and effort; however, most agree the need to decrease distance is there.

Cantlay is among the few, including Bryson DeChambeau, who think there isn't an issue with distance at all, but as every golf course continues to make changes to keep up with the modern game, that argument is getting harder to make.
